# bookmatch — Goodreads taste profiles and grounded book recommendations

## What it is

bookmatch is a Python application that turns a Goodreads account into a taste profile and a set of grounded book recommendations. It runs as a web service on aurora, exposed at port `:8092` via the systemd unit `bookmatch.service`, and serves a dark-theme single-page app from `static/`. The app package lives in `bookmatch/` with modules for analysis, neighbor search, agent interaction, the web app, and storage.

The pipeline starts with a one-time dataset build: `scripts/download_dataset.sh` fetches the UCSD Goodreads corpus (Wan & McAuley 2018) — roughly 6.5 GB — into `~/data/goodreads-ucsd/raw`, and `scripts/build_index.py` turns it into a neighbor-gap index under `~/data/goodreads-ucsd/index`. The index build reads four corpus files, keeps only rated interactions (ratings 1–5), and outputs a sparse rating matrix (`user_item.npz`), a SQLite book lookup (`book_lookup.sqlite`), and metadata (`meta.json`). The build is idempotent and rewrites the index directory each run.

At runtime, the service ingests a user's Goodreads shelf, computes taste axes, matches against the UCSD corpus, and produces a profile plus recommendations. A correctness surface, `books.v_bookmatch_correctness` (defined in `sql/v_bookmatch_correctness.sql`), asserts per account that the pipeline produced a grounded result: shelf ingested, taste axes complete, corpus matched, and non-empty recommendations and profile. The service depends on aurora-local services: Ollama (`nomic-embed-text`), the livingos-api gateway at `:8510`, and Postgres at `:5435`.

## Why it exists

Goodreads offers no way to derive meaningful insight from a reading history — the June-2026 "impossible insights" rec-engine was a one-off that bookmatch recreates as a durable MyApps app. Without it, a user has no grounded, explainable path from a Goodreads shelf to recommendations they can trust and veto.

## How it is used

- **Owner** — deploys via `./deploy.sh` (in-place restart of `bookmatch.service`, health-proved), runs `scripts/install_hooks.sh` once per fresh clone to activate the pre-push test gate, and runs `python3 -m bookmatch.storage` explicitly to bootstrap or upgrade the `books.*` schema.
- **Agent** — interacts through the web app at `:8092` and the capability manifest `capability.yaml` (`cap.bookmatch-recommend`), which is crawled into the capability registry.
- **Automatic consumers** — the correctness view `books.v_bookmatch_correctness` is the ADR-0071 surface that asserts a grounded result per account; CI (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`) runs the pytest suite on push/PR.

## Boundaries

- **Owns:** the Goodreads dataset download and index build; the taste-profile and recommendation pipeline; the `books.*` schema (bootstrapped only by `python3 -m bookmatch.storage`, never as an app-start or test side effect); the correctness assertion in `books.v_bookmatch_correctness`; the in-place deploy and rollback procedure.
- **Never does:** download or store the raw corpus inside the repo — the dataset is gitignored at `~/data/goodreads-ucsd/raw` because it is ~6.5 GB and not source code; create the `books.*` schema as a side effect of app start or tests — the app and test roles do not hold CREATE, so schema bootstrap is a deliberate, separate step; deploy from a dirty working tree — `deploy.sh` refuses, because an uncommitted change would make the live unit untraceable.
- **Escalates to owner:** any deploy that fails health (`/api/health` not `ok` or `corpus_ready`) — the script rolls back to last-known-good and exits non-zero, but the decision to re-deploy or investigate is the owner's; any schema migration that requires CREATE on the `livingos` database — the app and test roles cannot do it.
